hero.title: Stand up the
hero.text: Build the file, database, licensing, and internal web services on SBD-FS01, SBD-SQL01, SBD-APPS01, and SBD-WEB01 in VLAN 40, each reachable only by its documented service path. Follow the build, explore the dependencies, and keep the evidence.

scene.label: Interactive 3D lesson network showing SBD-FS01, SBD-SQL01, SBD-APPS01, and SBD-WEB01 on VLAN 40 with the collector SBD-SYSLOG01, the fleet, the Tier 1 seat SBD-ADMIN-SRV01, and the registered service paths between them.
scene.completeCaption: Four business services run on VLAN 40, each reachable only by its registered path: files from SBD-FS01, licensing and the application API on SBD-APPS01, HTTPS from SBD-WEB01, and a database that answers SBD-APPS01 alone.

nodes.name: SBD-FS01
nodes.title: SBD-FS01 · 10.0.40.10
nodes.description: Serves the role-based shares to the fleet over SMB 445, with signing required on the server and encryption on the sensitive share. Access-based enumeration shows each user only what their roles permit.

nodes.name: SBD-SQL01
nodes.title: SBD-SQL01 · 10.0.40.20
nodes.description: Runs the database engine as a group managed service account, with connections encrypted under its SBD Server Authentication certificate. SBD-APPS01 is its only caller; its host firewall refuses SBD-WEB01.

nodes.name: SBD-APPS01
nodes.title: SBD-APPS01 · 10.0.40.30
nodes.description: The network’s one SQL consumer. Lesson 3 builds the host, creates its application gMSA and grants it database access; lesson 4 builds its licensing service and the application API that SBD-WEB01 calls.

nodes.name: SBD-WEB01
nodes.title: SBD-WEB01 · 10.0.40.40
nodes.description: Domain-joined Linux running Apache, built on course 1.1’s chrony file, course 1.2’s client package and the SBD root, hardened against DISA’s Apache STIGs, and serving internal HTTPS with an SBD Server Authentication certificate. Its only back-end dependency is the application API on SBD-APPS01.

nodes.name: SBD-SYSLOG01
nodes.title: SBD-SYSLOG01 · 10.0.20.20
nodes.description: Built in course 1.3. SBD-WEB01’s syslog arrives over TLS on TCP 6514 (F07) from lesson 4; in lesson 5 the three Windows servers join SBD Event Sources and forward their security events (F17).

nodes.name: 50 Windows PCs
nodes.title: 50 Windows PCs · 10.0.80.100–199
nodes.description: Built in course 1.6. Users reach SBD-FS01’s shares, SBD-APPS01’s licensing port, and SBD-WEB01’s HTTPS page on their registered rows. SBD-SQL01 stays out of reach: the router denies the fleet on 1433.

nodes.name: SBD-ADMIN-SRV01
nodes.title: SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 · 10.0.60.20
nodes.description: Built in course 1.1, part 8. The Tier 1 seat: every build and check on the four servers runs in a session from here (rule A02), and lesson 5’s first baselines are run in Tier 1 sessions from it.

flows.label: TCP 1433 with TLS · the only SQL caller

stepTitles: Write the business service-path rows
Add each new server’s maintenance rows
Choose managed identities on the course 1.4 key
Create the role-based access groups
Plan the three server certificates
design.mistake: Writing only the permits. Without the explicit WEB01-to-SQL01 deny, nothing in the register records that the web tier has no database dependency — and because all four servers share VLAN 40, the router never sees that traffic, so SQL01’s host firewall rule has no row to point to.
design.network: All four VLAN 40 servers are planned on the Servers & data segment, beside the existing fleet on VLAN 80, the collector on VLAN 20 and the Tier 1 seat on VLAN 60. No service paths are live yet: this lesson writes the register rows they will follow.

control.name: Information Flow Enforcement
control.body: The register states which flows are approved before any service exists: fleet to web, web to the application API, and only the application tier to the database. Every host firewall rule and router permit built later enforces a row written here.
control.question: Which row would you struggle to justify if a reviewer asked why that flow needs to exist?

checklist: I wrote the service-path rows and WEB01’s repository and syslog rows, with SQL01 reachable only from APPS01 and an explicit WEB01-to-SQL01 deny.
I confirmed the course 1.4 KDS root key is the forest’s only one and created the per-share and per-application role groups under the Groups OU.
I planned an SBD Server Authentication certificate for SQL01, APPS01, and WEB01, each to be requested on its own host.

stepTitles: Build SBD-FS01 in the Servers OU
Create shares with role-group NTFS permissions
Enable access-based enumeration
Require SMB signing and encrypt the sensitive share
Test access and denial for two roles
fileserver.mistake: Trusting the defaults. The newest Windows Server release requires SMB signing only for its own outbound connections, so SBD-FS01 does not require it from clients until you set RequireSecuritySignature in its SMB server configuration. Confirm it on a live connection, not just in the setting.
fileserver.network: SBD-FS01 is live on VLAN 40, and the fleet reaches it over SMB 445 on its registered row, signed or encrypted. The other three servers are still planned.

control.name: Access Enforcement
control.body: NTFS permissions granted to role groups decide who can open each share, and access-based enumeration hides what a role cannot open. The two-role test shows enforcement in both directions: access granted, and access refused and recorded as event 5145.
control.question: If a user changes jobs tomorrow, what single change moves their file access, and where is it recorded?

checklist: I joined SBD-FS01 into the Servers OU with time from a domain controller, and granted share and NTFS permissions to role groups only.
I confirmed RequireSecuritySignature is True on SBD-FS01 and checked Signed or Encrypted on a live connection from a fleet machine.
I tested two roles from fleet machines, saw each other’s shares stay invisible and denied, and found each refusal recorded as event 5145.

stepTitles: Build SQL01 and APPS01’s host, then the gMSAs
Request the certificate and force encryption
Grant database roles to APPS01’s identity only
Prove one caller in and both refusals
database.mistake: Testing only the permitted connection. APPS01 connecting proves the permit; without the refused attempts from a VLAN 40 neighbour and a fleet machine, and dropped-packet logging turned on in SQL01’s host firewall, nothing shows the one-caller rule is enforced.
database.network: SBD-SQL01 is live, and SBD-APPS01’s application identity connects to it on TCP 1433 with TLS, the only registered SQL path. The refused attempts from SBD-FS01, at SQL01’s host firewall, and from the fleet, at the router, are not permitted paths, so no flow is shown for them.

control.name: Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity | Cryptographic Protection
control.body: The SBD Server Authentication certificate bound to the instance, with encrypted connections required, protects every query between SBD-APPS01 and SBD-SQL01. The urlfetch check shows the chain validating against pki.sbd.test like every other certificate on this network.
control.question: What evidence shows the connection is encrypted in practice, not only configured to be?

checklist: I created one gMSA per service, each allowed to one computer, and confirmed the database service runs as its gMSA.
I bound the server certificate, forced encrypted connections, and recorded the certutil urlfetch output.
I recorded APPS01’s successful connection with the refused attempts from SBD-FS01 and a fleet machine and their log entries.

stepTitles: Run APPS01’s licensing service and application API
Build SBD-WEB01 on domain time, the SBD root and SBD-REPO01
Join the domain, scope the firewall, send syslog
Serve HTTPS from a hardened Apache
Prove the chain and the closed shortcuts
apps-web.mistake: Pointing the web application straight at the database “just for now.” A connection string from WEB01 to SQL01 breaks the three-tier design, and SQL01’s host firewall refuses it anyway: the web tier reaches data only through the application API on SBD-APPS01.
apps-web.network: Every VLAN 40 service is live. The fleet reaches SBD-WEB01 on HTTPS 443 and SBD-APPS01 on its licensing port, SBD-WEB01 calls the application API on SBD-APPS01 and sends its syslog to SBD-SYSLOG01 over TLS, and SBD-APPS01 alone queries SBD-SQL01.

control.name: Configuration Settings
control.body: SBD-WEB01’s Apache configuration is hardened against DISA’s Apache STIGs, exported, and hashed. The export records what the settings are, the hash shows later whether they changed, and lesson 5 measures the whole host with SCC for Linux.
control.question: Which hardening items did you mark not applicable or leave open, and is the reason for each written down?

checklist: I verified APPS01’s licensing path from the fleet and its application API answering SBD-WEB01 over HTTPS.
I built SBD-WEB01 on course 1.1’s chrony file, course 1.2’s client package and the SBD root, joined it with SSSD, saw its syslog reach the collector, and hashed its hardened Apache configuration.
I loaded the HTTPS page from a fleet machine with a validating chain and recorded the refused WEB01-to-SQL01 attempt.

stepTitles: Enrol the three Windows servers with the collector
Reconcile the full register against live behavior
Baseline all four hosts
Update inventory, register, and exceptions
Write the handoff to course 1.12
prove-scan.mistake: Stopping at the scan output. A baseline only closes the course once each open item is classified — fix by GPO (fix now on SBD-WEB01), deviation candidate, or POA&M candidate — and any service-hardening deviation you keep goes to the exception record’s owner.
prove-scan.network: All four VLAN 40 servers are live with every registered path shown. The three Windows servers now forward their events to SBD-SYSLOG01 beside SBD-WEB01’s syslog, and each host’s first baseline runs in a Tier 1 session from SBD-ADMIN-SRV01. The adjacent denies, including WEB01 to SQL01, are probed and logged rather than drawn.

control.name: Baseline Configuration
control.body: Each new host’s first SCAP baseline — SCC with the Windows Server benchmark on three of them, SCC for Linux on SBD-WEB01 — records its measured state, and the classified findings say what changes next. Later rescans compare against it, so drift becomes visible.
control.question: Which open item would you fix before course 1.12 begins backing up these servers, and which needs a documented decision instead?

checklist: I enrolled SBD-FS01, SBD-SQL01, and SBD-APPS01 in SBD Event Sources and saw their events, and SBD-WEB01’s syslog, on the collector.
I reconciled every VLAN 40 row with paired permit and deny proof, including WEB01 to SQL01.
I baselined all four hosts, classified their open items, turned their inventory rows active, and wrote the handoff note.
